== Sole citizenship (P27) claim is unsourced, and doesn't reflect his documented birth/origin ==

Also a request for editors to double-check, not a confirmed error — same
spirit as the Popper/Szymanowska/Barrie note in this directory.

[[Q4453717]] carries exactly one {{P|27}} (citizenship) value: Russian
Empire ([[Q34266]]), with '''no reference attached to the claim at all'''.
No other citizenship claim exists on the item — nothing for the Austrian
Empire, Bohemia, or any entity matching where he was actually born.

The independent Jewish Encyclopedia entry (linked above) states he was born
in Prague in 1817 (then part of the Austrian Empire) and studied there under
Wenzel Tomaschek, only settling in Odesa — within the Russian Empire — in
1840, as an adult, for his career. Prague/Bohemia does not appear anywhere
in his Wikidata claims, even though it's his place of birth and musical
training.

We found this while cross-referencing his citizenship for a nationality
classification of our own and initially assigned "Russian" purely by
trusting this claim at face value, before the lack of a source and the
mismatch with his documented biography prompted a second look.

'''Suggested fix (for Wikidata editors to judge, not something we can do
ourselves):''' either add a {{P|27}}=Austrian Empire ([[Q28513]]) claim
reflecting his birth/origin (the existing Russian Empire claim would still
be correct for his later, adult citizenship — both can coexist, as is
already the pattern for many composers of this era on Wikidata), or at
minimum attach a source to the existing claim so its basis is checkable.

(For context: our own database now records him as Austrian rather than
Russian, based on the Jewish Encyclopedia source above, since that's the
better-supported description of his primary origin/identity — not a claim
that Wikidata's Russian Empire citizenship is factually wrong, just that
it's unsourced and tells only part of the story.)
